notes: The Arduino Nano 33 BLE is not in the catalogue, so it is a new part type with only the pins used here: GND, A4 (SDA), A5 (SCL), 3V3 (labelled '3V' in the image).

The diagram shows no breadboard, but the manual lists mini breadboards. I used one breadboard (bb1) as the junction where the SDA lines, SCL lines and pull-up resistors meet. This is an assumption. The electrical topology matches the image.

In the image, the teal (A5/SCL) line of both boards joins one 4.7k resistor. The yellow (A4/SDA) line of both boards joins the other 4.7k resistor. The other end of each resistor goes to the red 3V3 line from the reader. The GND line runs directly between the two boards.
I2C pins follow the manual: SDA is A4 and SCL is A5.
Both boards are powered and programmed over USB from a computer. The computer is not a part in the graph, so the USB cables only have a joined edge to their board.
The manual lists 10 jumper wires, but the diagram needs only 6 wires, and the resistors are placed directly. I modelled only the 6 wires the diagram needs.
The breadboard column and rail positions (10t, 12t, tp.1-3) are arbitrary. Only the connectivity matters.
